title: Investigate asymmetric replay credit leak impacting hybrid routing
creator: Nadia Patel
description: Multiple customers reported unexplained metering increases after hybrid routing failovers (hosted -> dedicated/private fallback). The symptom: token/billing delta grows after transient capacity constraints; affected customers see net token credits charged without corresponding request traces in ledger. Initial triage suggests an interaction between async prefetch/replay on the edge proxy and the central metering aggregator where replayed tokens were not always deduplicated or were double-attributed when fallback routing occurred.
steps_taken: 2025-02-14: Eng on-call reproduced spike in lower environment by simulating fallback routing and enabling prefetch replay
Captured proxy traces for request lifecycle (edge -> router -> runtime) and compared per-request request_id vs billing ledger entries
Added temporary debug logging for replay headers X-RW-REPLAY-ID and X-RW-ORIG-ROUTE in staging proxy and metering-forwarder
Queried metering DB for identical prompt hashes across routes: SELECT request_id, sum(tokens) FROM metering WHERE created_at > '2025-02-14' GROUP BY request_id HAVING sum(tokens) > 1
Throttled prefetch path in staging to observe effect on issuance of duplicate ledger entries
findings: Race condition: when fallback routing triggers mid-KV-replay window, the proxy issues a replay with a fresh request_id but preserves X-RW-REPLAY-ID leading to the aggregator treating it as a separate accounting event
Metering forwarder dedupe relies on (request_id) only; replayed requests sometimes receive new request_id due to proxy reconnects during failover, so dedupe missed duplicates

In some flows the retry path appended tokens to an existing session ledger entry instead of incrementing the replay origin entry, causing asymmetric attribution (customer A sees more tokens billed under tenant fallback ledger)
Issue appears only when: prefetch enabled + hybrid fallback + short-lived runtime eviction. Hosted-only flows unaffected.
Two customers (NovaHealth, AcmePay) surfaced the issue; internal alerting thresholds were insufficient to classify the anomalous delta as a billing-critical incident earlier.
proposed_fix: Patch proxy to preserve original request_id across replay attempts (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/4812)
Update metering forwarder to dedupe on composite key (orig_request_id OR replay_id) instead of request_id only (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/2305)
Add idempotency token header X-RW-IDEMPOTENCY to replay path and persist in ledger ingestion pipeline
Backfill script to reconcile affected ledgers by matching on replay_id and prompt-hash (runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Replay+Reconciliation)
Short-term configuration: disable prefetch replay for hybrid-routed tenants until the patch rolls out
rollout_plan: Stage patch to staging cluster and run synthetic hybrid-failover workload for 24h
Canary deploy to 10% of affected tenants in production (monitor: billing-delta, request_id-dup rate) with automatic rollback on >2% delta
Full rollout to all regions after 72h of stable canary metrics
After successful rollout, run backfill reconciliation and apply credits to impacted tenants with clear customer comms
